    Create a custom module

    You can develop custom toolbar modules tailored to your project environment by implementing the IToolbarModule interface. Toolbar scripts should be created under an Editor folder.

    Choose the API for your Unity version

    Read ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt and use the implementation that matches m_EditorVersion.

    Unity version Module implementation
    6000.3 or newer Implement IToolbarModule. Declare UI with Unity's official MainToolbarElement API.
    2022.3 through 6000.2 Implement IToolbarModule and ILegacyToolbarModule. Add UI through LegacyToolbarBuilder.

    Custom Toolbar does not support Unity versions earlier than 2022.3.

    Register the module

    Module registration works the same way across all supported Unity versions. Every module needs a stable, globally unique ID and must register exactly once from an [InitializeOnLoad] static constructor.

    using NKStudio.CustomToolbar;
using UnityEditor;

[InitializeOnLoad]
internal sealed class ExampleToolbarModule : IToolbarModule
{
    private const string ModuleId = "Company.Product.Toolbar.Example";

    static ExampleToolbarModule()
    {
        ToolbarModuleRegistry.Register(new ExampleToolbarModule());
    }

    public string Id => ModuleId;

    public void Refresh(ToolbarRefreshReason reason)
    {
        // Refresh this module's toolbar state.
    }
}

    Do not subscribe separately to EditorApplication.playModeStateChanged or EditorBuildSettings.sceneListChanged. The toolbar host sends the corresponding ToolbarRefreshReason to registered modules.

    Unity 6000.3 or newer

    Use Unity's public Main Toolbar API. The path passed to MainToolbar.Refresh must exactly match the path declared by MainToolbarElement.

    using NKStudio.CustomToolbar;
using UnityEditor;
using UnityEditor.Toolbars;

[InitializeOnLoad]
internal sealed class ModernExampleToolbarModule : IToolbarModule
{
    private const string ModuleId = "Company.Product.Toolbar.Example";
    private const string ElementPath = "Company Toolbar/Example";

    static ModernExampleToolbarModule()
    {
        ToolbarModuleRegistry.Register(new ModernExampleToolbarModule());
    }

    public string Id => ModuleId;

    public void Refresh(ToolbarRefreshReason reason)
    {
        if (reason is ToolbarRefreshReason.Initialized or ToolbarRefreshReason.PlayModeChanged)
            MainToolbar.Refresh(ElementPath);
    }

    [MainToolbarElement(
        ElementPath,
        defaultDockPosition = MainToolbarDockPosition.Right,
        defaultDockIndex = 20)]
    private static MainToolbarElement CreateElement()
    {
        var content = new MainToolbarContent("Example", "Run an Editor action.");
        return new MainToolbarButton(content, OnClick)
        {
            enabled = ToolbarAvailability.InEditMode
        };
    }

    private static void OnClick()
    {
        // Run an Editor-only action.
    }
}

    Unity 2022.3 through 6000.2 compatibility

    For earlier supported versions, implement ILegacyToolbarModule and create UI Toolkit controls in BuildLegacy. The package owns all toolbar reflection.

    using NKStudio.CustomToolbar;
using UnityEditor;
using UnityEditor.UIElements;

[InitializeOnLoad]
internal sealed class LegacyExampleToolbarModule : IToolbarModule, ILegacyToolbarModule
{
    private const string ModuleId = "Company.Product.Toolbar.Example";
    private ToolbarButton _button;

    static LegacyExampleToolbarModule()
    {
        ToolbarModuleRegistry.Register(new LegacyExampleToolbarModule());
    }

    public string Id => ModuleId;

    public void Refresh(ToolbarRefreshReason reason)
    {
        _button?.SetEnabled(ToolbarAvailability.InEditMode);
    }

    public void BuildLegacy(LegacyToolbarBuilder builder)
    {
        _button = new ToolbarButton(OnClick) { text = "Example" };
        _button.SetEnabled(ToolbarAvailability.InEditMode);
        builder.Add(LegacyToolbarZone.Right, _button);
    }

    private static void OnClick()
    {
        // Run an Editor-only action.
    }
}

    Add every element through LegacyToolbarBuilder.Add. Available zones are Left, CenterLeft, CenterRight, and Right.

    Validation checklist

    • Confirm the module ID is not duplicated in Assets or Packages.
    • Keep the action Editor-only and use ToolbarAvailability.InEditMode for controls that must be disabled in Play Mode.
    • For Unity 6000.3 or newer, use the exact same element path for the attribute and refresh call.
    • For earlier supported versions, add every element through LegacyToolbarBuilder.
    • Compile and test with the Unity version recorded in ProjectVersion.txt.

    Choose the enabled state of a toolbar element

    ToolbarAvailability provides four properties for the enabled value of a toolbar element. Choose the property whose name matches the intended behavior instead of interpreting a negated condition.

    Property When the element is enabled Use case
    InEditMode In Edit Mode Editor actions that must not run in Play Mode or while entering Play Mode
    InPlayMode During actual Play Mode Actions available only while the game is running
    Always Always Actions available regardless of the Editor state
    Never Never Visible actions that are not currently available

    On Unity 6000.3 or newer, assign the desired property to enabled in the element factory. The following button is enabled only in Edit Mode.

    [MainToolbarElement(
    ElementPath,
    defaultDockPosition = MainToolbarDockPosition.Right,
    defaultDockIndex = 20)]
private static MainToolbarElement CreateElement()
{
    var content = new MainToolbarContent("Example", "Run an Editor action.");

    return new MainToolbarButton(content, OnClick)
    {
        enabled = ToolbarAvailability.InEditMode
    };
}

    When using InEditMode or InPlayMode, recreate the element during initialization and whenever the Play Mode state changes.

    public void Refresh(ToolbarRefreshReason reason)
{
    if (reason is ToolbarRefreshReason.Initialized or ToolbarRefreshReason.PlayModeChanged)
        MainToolbar.Refresh(ElementPath);
}
    Tip

    ModernToolbarHost sends ToolbarRefreshReason.PlayModeChanged to every registered module whenever the Play Mode state changes. If the module is registered with ToolbarModuleRegistry, its state updates without a separate EditorApplication.playModeStateChanged subscription.

    Always and Never do not change with Play Mode, so they do not require recreation for state changes.

    Display a dynamic value in a label

    To display an external value in a toolbar label, as the Scene Switcher does, read the value inside CreateElement(). The first argument of the MainToolbarContent constructor is the label shown in the toolbar.

    private static MainToolbarElement CreateElement()
{
    string label = MyToolbarData.CurrentLabel;

    var content = new MainToolbarContent(
        label,
        "Display the current value.");

    return new MainToolbarButton(content, OnClick)
    {
        enabled = ToolbarAvailability.InEditMode
    };
}

    The asset's built-in Scene Switcher displays the name of the first enabled scene in Build Settings. Its core structure is as follows.

    public void Refresh(ToolbarRefreshReason reason)
{
    if (reason is ToolbarRefreshReason.Initialized
        or ToolbarRefreshReason.SceneListChanged)
    {
        MainToolbar.Refresh(ElementPath);
    }
}

[MainToolbarElement(ElementPath)]
private static MainToolbarElement CreateElement()
{
    string label = $"Start '{SceneHelper.FirstSceneName}'";

    return new MainToolbarButton(
        new MainToolbarContent(label, "Start the first scene in Build Settings."),
        SceneHelper.MoveFirstScene)
    {
        enabled = ToolbarAvailability.InEditMode
            && SceneHelper.HasFirstScene
    };
}
    Important

    A label does not change automatically when its source value changes. CreateElement() uses the value available when the element is created, so call MainToolbar.Refresh(ElementPath) in response to the source value's change event to apply the new label.

    SceneHelper is the class that retrieves and formats values for the asset's built-in Scene Switcher. Follow the same pattern in a custom module: keep data handling in a separate Helper or Provider class, and let the toolbar class focus on presenting that value.
